**This is a pre-release for testing.** It is not marked Latest and is not intended for general use. If you want a stable build, use [v0.5.0](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/releases/tag/v0.5.0).

This is the second beta of 0.5.1. Since beta.1 it changes one thing: **night lighting no longer lights the ground right around the aircraft**, and leaves it to X-Plane's own 3D lights, because XEarthLayer's street lamps were too coarse up close. If you tested beta.1, see "Coming from beta.1" below.

0.5.1's biggest change is on macOS: **XEarthLayer no longer uses macFUSE's kernel extension.** It mounts its scenery through macFUSE's FSKit backend instead, so a new Mac no longer has to boot into Recovery and lower its security. On every platform, night lighting now draws **street lamps along real roads**, cities are lit closer to what you see from the air, and a new **`network.connections`** setting keeps XEarthLayer from overwhelming home routers.

| Platform | Download |
|---|---|
| Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.34 or newer) | `xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.2-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` |
| macOS 15.4 or newer, Apple Silicon | `xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.2-arm64-macos.pkg`, Homebrew (below), or `xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.2-arm64-macos.tar.gz` |

No `.deb`, `.rpm` or AUR package is built for previews. There is no Intel Mac build; Intel Mac users can build from source. The `xearthlayer-publish` downloads are the package publishing tool, which testers do not need.

---

## Setup

Close X-Plane and stop any running XEarthLayer before you start.

### 1. macOS only: set up macFUSE for FSKit

This build needs **macOS 15.4 or later** and **macFUSE 5.3.3 or later**. [docs/macos.md](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/blob/develop/0.5.1/docs/macos.md) walks through each step.

1. Install or update [macFUSE](https://macfuse.io). If you already have 5.3.3 or later, keep it.
2. Open **System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions**, click the ⓘ next to **File System Extensions**, and turn on **macFUSE (local)**. System Settings may list both **macFUSE** and **macFUSE (local)**; XEarthLayer needs **macFUSE (local)**.
3. If X-Plane is on an **external drive** (under `/Volumes`):
   - Give `/usr/libexec/fskitd` Full Disk Access under **Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access** (click **+**, press `Cmd+Shift+G` and type the path).
   - The drive must have ownership turned on. XEarthLayer checks this when it starts, and if ownership is off it stops and prints the `sudo diskutil enableOwnership` command for your drive.

Coming from 0.5.0? You no longer need the kernel extension you approved for it. Steps 1 and 2 are still needed: the kernel extension approval does not turn on the file system extension.

### 2. Install the binary

**Linux:**

```bash
tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.2-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.1-beta.2
```

**macOS**, choose **one** of the three ways below.

**With the installer package.** Download `xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.2-arm64-macos.pkg`, double-click it and follow the Installer. It puts `xearthlayer` in `/usr/local/bin`, which is already on your `PATH`. The package is signed and notarized with the ticket attached, so it installs without a network connection. In a new terminal:

```bash
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.1-beta.2
```

**With Homebrew.** The pre-release channel follows every alpha, beta and rc build:

```bash
brew install --cask xearthlayer/tap/xearthlayer@prerelease
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.1-beta.2
```

If macFUSE is already installed from its own installer, add `--skip-cask-deps`. Already on the channel? `brew upgrade --cask xearthlayer/tap/xearthlayer@prerelease` is all you need.

**From the tarball.** Safari unpacks the download into a folder for you (`cd ~/Downloads/xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.2-arm64-macos`); with any other browser, `cd ~/Downloads` and `tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.2-arm64-macos.tar.gz`. Then:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.1-beta.2
```

If `xearthlayer --version` prints something else, an older copy comes first on your `PATH`: `which -a xearthlayer` lists every copy.

### Coming from beta.1?

Install the binary (step 2) and run. Nothing in your configuration changes, and the night lighting beta.1 saved on disk stays valid.

### 3. Coming from 0.5.0 or a 0.5.0 preview?

Your configuration and packages carry over. Bring the configuration up to date:

```bash
xearthlayer config upgrade
```

It adds the new `[network]` section and removes `fuse.macos_backend`, which no longer exists. Nothing else changes, so go to step 5.

**One default changes for everyone:** `network.connections` is `high`, so XEarthLayer now opens a third fewer connections than 0.5.0 did. If you have prosumer or enterprise network hardware and want 0.5.0's limits back, `xearthlayer config set network.connections max`. See "What we most want tested" below.

### 4. New to XEarthLayer, or coming from v0.4.8?

Run `xearthlayer setup`. It asks for the new network connections level as step 4: **High** suits most home routers, **Max** needs prosumer or enterprise network hardware, and **Low** is for older or low spec routers. When it finishes it offers to open the package manager, where you install the regions you fly (press `2` for the Library, mark regions with `Space`, press `i`).

Coming from v0.4.8, follow the upgrade steps in the [v0.5.0 release notes](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/releases/tag/v0.5.0) first: the rebuilt world replaces the old one, and the old packages must be removed before new ones are installed.

### 5. Run

```bash
xearthlayer run
```

---

## What changed since beta.1

- **Night lighting leaves the ground right around the aircraft to X-Plane.** On the textures nearest the aircraft, beta.1 drew XEarthLayer's lit layer under X-Plane's 3D scenery at a twelfth of its light, street lamps included. Up close those lamps were too coarse and did not line up with X-Plane's own road lights. That nearest level is black again, as in 0.5.0: the lit layer fades to a quarter of its light as you close in, and X-Plane's 3D lights light the ground beneath you.

## What changed since 0.5.0

**macOS**

- **No kernel extension.** XEarthLayer mounts through macFUSE's FSKit backend only. There is no Recovery step and no kernel extension approval, and the `fuse.macos_backend` setting is gone.
- **External drives.** At startup, XEarthLayer checks that the drive holding X-Plane honours ownership, and recreates its mount folder if it is empty, because FSKit refuses a folder made while ownership was off. A failed mount now names the likely causes rather than only macFUSE's `os error 35`.
- **Quitting leaves nothing mounted.** `q`, Ctrl+C and SIGTERM unmount the scenery, and a Ctrl+C during the first seconds of startup now does too (on Linux as well).
- **`xearthlayer diagnostics` has a macFUSE section**: the macFUSE version, whether its FSKit framework is present, and XEarthLayer's volume while it runs. The flight log records the same once after mounting.

**Night lighting**

- **Roads light up at night.** Motorways and main roads carry chains of street lamps, read from the road overlays and airport packs X-Plane loads in your `scenery_packs.ini` order, X-World Pro included. An area with no road overlay has no road lights, as it has no roads in the simulator.
- **Close to the aircraft, X-Plane's lights take over.** The lit layer fades to a quarter of its light as you close in and then leaves the ground beneath you to X-Plane's 3D lights.
- **Cities are whiter.** Most neighbourhoods are now LED white, the remaining sodium districts a softer amber, and distant towns keep their light and colour instead of fading to orange.
- Night lighting saved on disk by 0.5.0 is generated again the first time it is needed, so the first night flight in each area does more work.

**Network**

- **`network.connections` (`max`, `high`, `low`)** sets how many connections XEarthLayer opens: for imagery X-Plane is waiting on, for prefetch, kept open to the imagery servers, and for package downloads. The default is `high`.

**Dashboard**

- The headless status line, the panic report and the telemetry summary count the tiles being generated right now. The count was always 0, and it now reads "running".
- The Prefetch pane's meter is labelled **Utilization** and has a twelve-second sparkline.
- On Linux, "Authorization required, but no authorization protocol specified" no longer appears over the dashboard when the shell has a stale `DISPLAY`.

## What we most want tested

### 1. macOS: FSKit from start to finish

This is the change that most needs real Macs. Set up macFUSE as in step 1, then tell us:

- Did the steps work as written, especially turning on **macFUSE (local)**? Did anything ask for approval that the notes do not mention?
- Does `xearthlayer run` mount and serve scenery, and does `xearthlayer diagnostics` show `Mounted: FSKit` while it runs?
- With X-Plane on an external drive: did the Full Disk Access step and the ownership check behave as described?
- Quit with `q`, with Ctrl+C, and once during startup. Afterwards, `mount | grep zzXEL` should print nothing.

### 2. `network.connections` on your network

- If XEarthLayer ever made your router, modem or Wi-Fi drop out, try `high` (the default) and then `low`, and tell us your router model and which level stays stable.
- On a fast connection with capable equipment, tell us whether `high` loads scenery noticeably slower than `max` did in 0.5.0, for example at the first scene load or a boundary crossing.

### 3. Night flights

Fly over cities and along motorways at night, low as well as high. Close in, does the hand-off from XEarthLayer's light to X-Plane's 3D lights look natural, or do you see a dark ring or a visible edge around the aircraft? Farther out, do the road lamps line up with the roads X-Plane draws? Are there lamps where there is no road, or roads with no lamps that should have them? Does the city colour look right from the air? Screenshots help, with the location.

### 4. Your normal flights

Fly your usual routes and tell us about anything that would stop you recommending this build: pauses or purple tiles at DSF boundary crossings, slow starts, missing scenery, or SimHeaven X-World Pro misbehaving with `packages.xworld_pro` on.

## How to report

The flight log is `xearthlayer.log`, and the package manager's log is `xearthlayer-packages.log`, both at `~/.local/state/xearthlayer/` on Linux and in `~/Library/Logs/XEarthLayer/` on macOS unless you changed `logging.file`. `xearthlayer run` empties the flight log when it starts, so copy it before the next flight. Then run:

```bash
xearthlayer --version
xearthlayer diagnostics
```

The most useful report is your route, aircraft and flight time, the last few `Prefetch sample` lines from the flight log, and what looked wrong. For a network report, include your router or modem model, your connection speed, and the `Network connections` line near the top of the flight log.

**On macOS, if the mount fails**, macFUSE's own message (`os error 35`) rarely says why. The reason is in the system log; run this right after the failure and include its output:

```bash
/usr/bin/log show --last 5m --predicate 'process == "fskitd"'
```

---

## Known issues, please don't report these

**FUSE read counts on the dashboard are low on macOS.** macOS serves repeat reads of a texture from its own cache, so XEarthLayer only sees the first one. Nothing else depends on that count.

**Saving a setting rewrites `config.ini` from its template.** Comments you added to the file by hand are lost, as they are with `xearthlayer config set`. The values are kept.

**Antarctica is not in the library yet.**
